title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Context, reconstructed from pages 55 and 57. J is a 3-element set, presumably with constant form J_S. V_J = F_2^J/F_2 (diagonal) is a Klein four-group, which page 57 identifies with the 2-torsion 2E_0 of an elliptic curve. Σ_J is the line Σ y_i = 0 in P^J, a P^1 with the three marked points y_i = 0. Σ*_J is the conic Σ x_i^2 = 0, on which V_J acts by sign changes. The map x ↦ y = x^2 makes Σ*_J → Σ_J the Galois (Z/2)^2-cover of P^1, branched with index 2 over the three points. Combinatorially this is the cover X(4) → X(2) of modular curves, or the 'Legendre' picture. A general object (X, I) is a twist of this universal cover by a V-torsor K: X ≅ K ∧^V Σ*_J. It carries a section x of Σ_J (the 'point at infinity'). The fibre over x is I, and relation (14) reads I ≅ K ∧_V (Σ*_J | x). This page does one rigidification step. Assume I is constant, I = I_S, and add the extra structure (15): a V_S-equivariant isomorphism between the fibre of X over the section and I_S. Translated to K this becomes (16): K ≅ I_S ∧_V (Σ*_{J,x}), with V = (V_J)_S. Formally one expects K ≅ I ∧ (Σ*_x)^{-1}. But V is commutative of exponent 2, so every V-torsor is canonically isomorphic to its own inverse, and the contracted product with Σ*_x itself is correct. A first, struck-out version of (16) wrote the subscript as V_{J_S}; it was replaced by underline V = (V_J)_S. The purpose: parametrize these level-2-type data by sections x of Σ_J, i.e. points of the λ-line minus the cusps. This prepares §3 (next page), where X arises as E/σ for an elliptic torsor E with the involution σx = a − x, whose fixed-point scheme is a 2E_0-torsor.
errors: No genuine error. (16) relies tacitly on the fact that torsors under the exponent-2 group V are self-inverse; otherwise one would need (Σ*_x)^{-1}. The correction of the subscript from V_{J_S} to V = (V_J)_S is notational only.

ideas.what: Twisting the universal Klein-four cover of P^1 branched at 3 points by a V-torsor, and rigidifying by trivializing the fibre over a section, which pins down the torsor K
ideas.modern_name: Twisted forms / contracted products of torsors; full level-2 (Legendre) structure; X(4)→X(2) as a (Z/2)^2-cover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Giraud's non-abelian cohomology, SGA1 descent; Legendre/Igusa for level-2 moduli; Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur)
ideas.where_published: Contracted products of torsors: SGA1, SGA3 and Giraud's book based on Grothendieck's ideas; the elliptic level-2 specifics are not in his published texts

deep.surprise_reason: Short page of routine torsor bookkeeping (a rigidification step) inside a standard description of level-2 moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2. Nothing new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: The first word is not 'd'identifiant'; the image reads something like 'di'chuisant' — perhaps 's'enrichissant' or 'rigidifiant' ('… par la structure supplémentaire').
The '∫' inserted above 'structure supplémentaire' is probably a caret or insertion mark, not an integral.
In (15) and (16), 't' / 'Σ*_{J,2} | t' is most likely the section x: read 'X|x ≃ I_S' and 'Σ*_{J}|x' (fibre at the section x), consistent with (14) on p.55.
Text: 'qui, en termes du V_S-torseur K qui est censé définir X, s'écrit' — fine.
The struck-out first version of (16) carried the subscript V_{J_S} (with 'S' scribbles); the final version reads K ≃ (I_S) ∧_{V} (Σ*_{J,x} | x) with V = (V_J)_S.
